title: Top normal local cohomology classes and general residue transitions
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $n\geq1$, $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$, and $X$ a Noetherian excellent scheme with $\ell$ invertible [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Use ordinary etale derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Geometric points, costalks $R\Gamma_{\bar x}$, roots-of-unity twists, and immediate normalized residue transitions are as in [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex]. For every geometric specialization $\bar y\rightsquigarrow\bar x$ of finite codimension $c$ (the dimension of the reduced closure of $\bar y$ in the strict localization at $\bar x$), every $M\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$, and every $a\in\mathbf Z$, there are canonical maps
$$\operatorname{sp}^X_{\bar y,\bar x}:H^a(R\Gamma_{\bar y}M)\longrightarrow H^{a+2c}(R\Gamma_{\bar x}M(c)).$$
They are natural in $M$, agree with the normalized immediate transitions when $c=1$ and with transport along the specified geometric specialization when $c=0$ (the identity for an identity specialization), commute with etale and strict-local restriction, and compose under chains of specializations, including the indicated Tate twists.

If $S$ is a Noetherian excellent normal strictly henselian local scheme of dimension $d$, with closed point $s$ and $\ell$ invertible [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring, def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], then
$$H^q_s(S,\Lambda(d))=0\quad(q>2d),\qquad [s]:\Lambda\xrightarrow{\sim}H^{2d}_s(S,\Lambda(d)).$$
The classes $[s]$ are invariant under the automorphisms of the chosen geometric points and commute with etale localization. On a normal integral excellent scheme, writing $r_x=\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}$, the corresponding geometric classes $c_{\bar x}\in H^{2r_x}(R\Gamma_{\bar x}\Lambda(r_x))$ satisfy
$$\operatorname{sp}_{\bar y,\bar x}(c_{\bar y})=c_{\bar x}$$
for every immediate geometric specialization, where $r_x=r_y+1$ and the source is twisted by $r_y$. At a geometric generic point the class is $1\in\Lambda$. Consequently the general specialization from a geometric generic point to $\bar x$ carries $1$ to $c_{\bar x}$.

source.place: Expose XVII, Theorems 3.1.1 and 3.1.2 and their proofs, especially 3.6.1 (invariance of the class); printed pp. 268, 277–280

proof.text: First choose a finite saturated chain between the generic and closed points of the reduced closure in the target strict localization. This is possible because its Krull dimension is finite; a maximal-length chain is saturated. Choose geometric lifts successively, retaining the specified generic specialization. The universal property of strict localization [lem-weil-pbc-map-into-henselian-colimit] factors the given map through each chosen strict localization; [lem-trf-ind-etale-strict-local-invariance] identifies its iterated strict localizations with the original ones. By [lem-per-immediate-specialization-criterion] the positive-codimension factors are immediate. Codimension-zero factors are the specified geometric transports. Compose the normalized immediate maps of [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex], with twists and shifts. Their naturality is part of the trait model in that definition. Write $P_c,Q_c$ for the chain-independence assertions of [lem-per-residue-chain-reductions]. That node reduces $P_c$ to $Q_c$. For $c\leq1$, two factorizations differ only by codimension-zero transports, and the immediate construction is compatible with those identifications. We prove $P_c$ by induction before proving the top-class assertion.

For $Q_2$, apply [lem-per-surface-resolution-supported-presentation]. Its exact presentation has generators $e_i$ and relations $d_z(e_i-e_j)$, with $d_z$ units. Connectedness of the intersection graph therefore identifies all generators in the cokernel; the sum-of-coefficients map identifies this cokernel with $\Lambda$. A normalized point class on any component gives its common generator. To compare resolutions, dominate both by a third as in that node. The common-domination and isomorphism-locus clauses of that node supply a closed point where pullback identifies the normalized point representatives. Thus the common generator in $H_s^4(S,\Lambda(2))$ is independent of the resolution. The node's flag formula says every two-step flag sends $1$ to that generator. Codimension-zero factors fix $1$, so $Q_2$ follows, and the reduction theorem gives $P_2$.

Let $c\geq3$ and suppose $P_{c-1}$. On a normal strictly henselian local $S$ of dimension $c$, for each $z\neq\eta,s$ compose the already defined transitions through a geometric lift of $z$ and apply the composite to $1$. Both positive codimensions are less than $c$. Conjugacy [lem-per-normal-geometric-specialization-conjugacy] and the fact that generic Galois automorphisms fix $1$ show that the resulting $\gamma_z\in H_s^{2c}(S,\Lambda(c))$ is independent of all lifts and factorizations. For comparable intermediate points $z\rightsquigarrow z'$, the induction hypothesis applied to the two shorter pieces gives $\gamma_z=\gamma_{z'}$. Given any $z,z'$, their nonzero prime ideals contain a common nonzero element $f$ (multiply one nonzero element from each). The punctured hypersurface $V(f)\setminus\{s\}$ is connected by [lem-per-normal-punctured-hypersurface-connected]. On each irreducible component, comparison with its generic point makes $\gamma$ constant; the finite component intersection graph is connected, so these constants agree. Thus all $\gamma_z$ agree. Every full flag has an intermediate point, hence $Q_c$ holds. [lem-per-residue-chain-reductions] now gives $P_c$, completing the induction.

source.place: XVII Lemma 3.5.8 and the conclusion of section 3.5

proof.text: The independent composite defines the asserted map for every complex and degree. Concatenation of factorizations proves composition, and naturality follows factor by factor. Composition is degree-correct because every factorization of a geometric specialization $\bar y\rightsquigarrow\bar x$ of codimension $c$ into codimension-zero and immediate factors has exactly $c$ immediate factors, so codimensions add. Indeed, the reduced closure $Z$ of the image of $\bar y$ in $X_{(\bar x)}$ is a local domain of dimension $c$; it is a quotient of the strict henselization of a localization of an excellent ring, hence Noetherian and excellent [lem-sc-strict-henselization-noetherian], [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent], [lem-exc-weakly-etale-excellent], [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability], so catenary [def-exc-excellent-ring]. The special points of the factors map to a chain of points of $Z$; a codimension-zero factor does not move the image point, and for an immediate factor $\bar z\rightsquigarrow\bar z'$ the identification of strict localizations [lem-trf-ind-etale-strict-local-invariance] and invariance of dimension [lem-sc-strict-henselization-dimension] show that the corresponding primes of $Z$ are adjacent. Thus the image chain is saturated from the generic to the closed point of $Z$, and by catenarity its length is $\dim Z=c$. For an etale or strict-local restriction, use [lem-per-prime-power-costalk-reduction] to compute each immediate factor on the same strict-local curve with the same normalized formula $d^{-1}\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde Z}(\nu^*i^!M)$ of [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex]. These computations have identical sources, targets and degree $d$, so their maps agree. Factorization independence proves restriction compatibility for the composite. Codimension zero is geometric transport; only an identity specialization necessarily gives the identity map.

First construct a class without asserting it is a generator. For a normal henselian local $S$ choose geometric generic and closed points and a specialization $t$, and put $c_{\bar s}=\operatorname{sp}_t(1)$. For $t'=t\sigma$, conjugacy [lem-per-normal-geometric-specialization-conjugacy] and composition from the transition construction in Steps 1–4 give $\operatorname{sp}_{t'}(1)=\operatorname{sp}_t(\sigma(1))=\operatorname{sp}_t(1)$. For a closed geometric automorphism $\tau$, use $\tau t=t\sigma$ to obtain $\tau(c_{\bar s})=c_{\bar s}$. An isomorphism of chosen generic geometric points has the same calculation. This proves independence and Galois invariance before any assertion on the size of the cohomology group. Step 4 also proves that these classes commute with etale localization.

The bound [lem-per-strict-local-etale-dimension-bounds] applied to the sheaf $\Lambda(d)$ gives $H_s^q(S,\Lambda(d))=0$ for $q>2d$. Prove that $1\mapsto c_{\bar s}$ is an isomorphism simultaneously for all such $S$, by induction on $d$. For $d=0$, normality says its local ring is a domain, and dimension zero makes its zero prime maximal, so it is a field; it is separably closed because $S$ is strictly henselian. The specialization is the identity and the assertion is $\Lambda=\Lambda$. For $d=1$, a normal one-dimensional Noetherian local ring is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-dim-one-iff-normal]. The potential pinning of $\Lambda$ in [lem-per-potential-dualizing-regular-unit] and its immediate compatibility give $\Lambda\xrightarrow{\sim}H_s^2(S,\Lambda(1))$, sending $1$ to the transition of $1$. For $d=2$, Step 2 already proved that every flag image of $1$ is the generator of the surface presentation, so the assertion holds. The remaining induction begins at $d\geq3$.

source.place: XVII, Proposition 3.2.1 and Section 2.4 (base dimensions 0 and 1)

proof.text: Fix $d\geq3$ and assume the assertion through dimension $d-1$. For $y\in U=S\setminus\{s\}$ put $p=\dim\mathcal O_{S,y}<d$. Its strict local scheme is Noetherian by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-noetherian], normal by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-colimit-normal-local-domain] applied to [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples], and of dimension $p$ by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-dimension]. Localization preserves excellence by [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent]; the strict localization is excellent by [lem-exc-weakly-etale-excellent] and [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability]. Apply the induction hypothesis there. Step 5 gives independence and invariance, so its top isomorphism is the isomorphism of residue-field sheaves $\Lambda\cong\mathcal H^{2p}(C_y\Lambda(p))$, not merely an isomorphism of one stalk. Its higher cohomology sheaves vanish. Thus all the local costalk hypotheses of [lem-per-coniveau-top-edge-presentation] hold.

source.place: XVII, proof of Lemma 3.6.2, first half

proof.text: For $y\in U^p$, the reduced closure $Z=\overline{\{y\}}\subset S$ is integral and strictly henselian local; it is a quotient of the excellent local ring of $S$. Excellence is preserved by [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent]. The strict henselian property of a quotient follows by lifting a simple-root polynomial to the original ring and lifting its root there; its residue field is unchanged. Catenarity in [def-exc-excellent-ring] gives $\dim Z=d-p$, by concatenating saturated chains through $y$. Apply the integral generic-point clause of [lem-per-strict-local-etale-dimension-bounds] to $Z$ to obtain the required bound $\operatorname{cd}_\ell\kappa(y)\leq d-p$. The coniveau theorem now gives a surjection $\bigoplus_{y\in U^{d-1}}H^1(\kappa(y),\Lambda(1))\twoheadrightarrow H_s^{2d}(S,\Lambda(d))$.

source.place: XVII, Proposition 3.2.2 and Lemma 3.6.2, spectral-sequence bounds

proof.text: Write $e_{\bar y}=\operatorname{sp}_{\bar\eta,\bar y}(1)$ for the lower-dimensional canonical class. The component formula in [lem-per-coniveau-top-edge-presentation] sends $b$ to $\epsilon\rho_y(b)\operatorname{sp}_{\bar y,\bar s}(e_{\bar y})$ with $\epsilon=\pm1$; only its image $\Lambda\operatorname{sp}_{\bar y,\bar s}(e_{\bar y})$ is used. By the transition construction in Steps 1–4 the latter transition of $e_{\bar y}$ is $\operatorname{sp}_{\bar\eta,\bar s}(1)=c_{\bar s}$; Step 5 removes the choice of the intermediate geometric lifts. Every component of the surjection in Step 8 therefore lands in $\Lambda c_{\bar s}$. Since that map is surjective, $\Lambda\to H_s^{2d}(S,\Lambda(d))$, $a\mapsto a c_{\bar s}$, is surjective. This argument proves the surjectivity part in dimension $d$ for every $S$, before starting its injectivity part.

Write $A=\mathcal O_S(S)$ and $\widehat A$ for its maximal-ideal completion. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], [lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete], [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring] and [lem-weil-pbc-completion-dimension], $\widehat A$ is complete Noetherian local, has the same residue field and dimension $d$, and is henselian by [lem-weil-pbc-complete-pair-henselian], hence strictly henselian. It is excellent by [lem-per-complete-local-excellence]. To verify normality, use that excellence makes $A$ a G-ring [def-exc-excellent-ring], [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]: the map $A\to\widehat A$ is flat with geometrically regular Noetherian fibres. The fibres are normal by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-normal]; [lem-weil-pbc-flat-normal-fibres-noetherian-normal] gives that $\widehat A$ is normal. Thus $\widehat S$ satisfies all hypotheses in the same dimension. [lem-per-completion-supported-constant-comparison] identifies its top cohomology module with that of $S$.

source.place: XVII, Lemma 3.6.3, completion reduction; Stacks 0C23 and 07QW

proof.text: Construct a testing potential complex on $\widehat S$. [lem-weil-pbc-cohen-power-series-presentation] gives a surjective local map $B\twoheadrightarrow\widehat A$ with $B$ complete Noetherian regular local and the same residue field. Hence $\ell$ is invertible in $B$; it is excellent by [lem-per-complete-local-excellence]. Put $i:\widehat S\hookrightarrow P=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $h=\dim\mathcal O_{P,i(\eta)}$. By [lem-per-potential-dualizing-regular-unit], $L=\Lambda_P(h)[2h]$ is potential for $h-\operatorname{codim}_P$. Set $K=i^!L$. The closed-immersion clause of [lem-per-prime-power-supported-calculus] identifies $C_xK$ with $C_{i(x)}L$, giving pinnings for the restricted dimension function. For an immediate specialization in $\widehat S$, its reduced strict-local curve and residue degree are identical to those in $P$; the finite-residue compatibility [lem-per-finite-residue-gysin-naturality], with identity residue-field maps, identifies its transition square with that of $L$. Thus these pinnings are potential. The generic dimension is zero by the definition of $h$, and the closed dimension is $-d$, by successive unit drops of the dimension function along a length-$d$ flag.

source.place: XVII Lemma 3.6.3; Proposition 2.4.3.1, Proposition 3.3.1 and Proposition 2.4.4.1 (closed-immersion case only)

proof.text: By [lem-per-normal-potential-low-degrees], the generic pinning of this $K$ extends to a map $f:\Lambda_{\widehat S}\to K$ equal to the identity at the geometric generic point. Naturality of the transition construction in Steps 1–4 gives a square with top row $\Lambda=H^0_{\bar\eta}\Lambda\to H^{2d}_{\bar s}(\Lambda(d))$, bottom row $H^0_{\bar\eta}K\to H^{2d}_{\bar s}(K(d))$, and vertical maps induced by $f$. The left map is an isomorphism. The bottom map is an isomorphism: factor the specialization, and use the compatibility of each immediate transition with the pinnings of [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex]; each is identified with the identity of $\Lambda$ after the indicated twists and shifts. Therefore if $a c_{\bar s}=0$ on $\widehat S$, the bottom isomorphism sends $a$ to zero, so $a=0$. Together with Step 9 (which applies also to $\widehat S$), this proves its top module is $\Lambda$.

source.place: XVII, Lemma 3.6.3, final commutative square, printed pp. 279–280

proof.text: The comparison of Step 10 consequently says that $H_s^{2d}(S,\Lambda(d))$ has exactly $\ell^n$ elements. Step 9 gives a surjection from the $\ell^n$-element module $\Lambda$ onto it. A surjection of two finite sets of the same cardinality has singleton fibres, hence is injective. This proves that $1\mapsto c_{\bar s}$ is an isomorphism for $S$ and completes the induction. Only an isomorphism of modules under completion was used; compatibility of the class with completion is not assumed.

On a normal integral excellent scheme, form the class at each geometric $\bar x$ in its normal strict localization. Its strict localization is Noetherian [lem-sc-strict-henselization-noetherian], a normal domain [lem-weil-pbc-etale-colimit-normal-local-domain] applied to [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples], excellent [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent], [lem-exc-weakly-etale-excellent], [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability], and of dimension $r_x$ [lem-sc-strict-henselization-dimension], so the result just proved gives $\Lambda\cong H^{2r_x}(C_{\bar x}\Lambda(r_x))$. For an immediate specialization $\bar y\rightsquigarrow\bar x$, concatenate a generic-to-$\bar y$ specialization with it. Composition in the transition construction in Steps 1–4 gives $\operatorname{sp}_{\bar y,\bar x}(c_{\bar y})=\operatorname{sp}_{\bar\eta,\bar x}(1)=c_{\bar x}$ with the source twisted by $r_y$. Here $r_x=r_y+1$: by [lem-per-immediate-specialization-criterion] the closure of $y$ has one-dimensional local ring at $x$, and $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is a catenary local domain [def-exc-excellent-ring], so a maximal chain of primes of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ through $y$ has length $r_y+1$, while every saturated chain of primes of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ has length $r_x$. Independence, automorphism invariance and etale compatibility are Step 5; the generic class is the identity transition of $1$. A finite immediate factorization and repeated application of this equality give the final general-specialization assertion.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q22-52ee35df0 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the delivery in full: the item, all eight new nodes, the statements of every cited node, and ILO XVII §3 (printed pp. 268–280) against the item. The proof follows ILO §3: 3.4 (surface case), 3.5.4–3.5.8 (chain reductions and the connectedness induction), 3.6.1 and 3.6.2–3.6.4 (completion and the test complex). It cites no SGA: connectedness comes from Stacks 0ECR on the completion, which is a normal domain by 0C23. The only statement change is c=0 'identity' replaced by 'transport', as the NW and Q42 reviewers asked; the old wording fails for a nontrivial Galois element. I checked closures: there is no cycle, and the delivery avoids higher-residue-transitivity and general-costalk-transitions, which both cite this item. All 8 new nodes are statement-only and true; none restates a clause of the item. I checked them on small cases: 0ECR with c=d≥3 and cd≤1, the E_1 bounds re-derived by hand, conjugacy via K-embeddings of Frac O^sh, dimension-bounds edge case e=0. I fixed three faults. (1) C1/E5, Step 4: composition needs codimension additivity, which the NW reviewer had required and the delivery never proved. Step 4 now proves it: the closure Z in X_(x̄) is excellent, so catenary; immediate factors give adjacent primes via 05WR and strict-henselization dimension, so the chain is saturated of length c. (2) C1, Step 14: the strict-local properties were uncited and r_x=r_y+1 was unargued. Step 14 now cites them and derives r_x=r_y+1 from the immediate criterion and catenarity of O_{X,x}. (3) E2 precaution: the coniveau node's codimension-one component formula pinned a sign that ILO never asserts (ILO states only the image). It now reads ε=±1 times ρ_y, and item Step 9 uses only the image. Batch-5 flags are all accepted as generic: the ind-étale strict-local invariance node (Stacks 05WR/0GIP), finite-base strict localization (Stacks 05WR/0GIP/04GH), the derivedPlus adjunction, and the stalk tensor via absolute-gysin-purity. None is a step of the trace formula or of Poincaré duality. I accept the 16 tool_uses (generic algebra). Maintainer notes: dimension-bounds is the Z/ℓ^n generalization of lem-per-punctured-support-cohomological-bound (F_ℓ, ILO 3.2.1), and the report misdescribes that node; conjugacy overlaps lem-trf-normal-generic-arrow-transitivity, stated for topos points; ILO 3.1.2 is still stated in three nodes. Fixes are in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-deligne-laumon-a1/ (the item and the coniveau node).; 2 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
